accepted.question_text: Let 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure such that the Banach space L^p(μ) is non-separable. Can L^p(μ) occur as a subspace of some Banach space that has an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1 (Enflo-Rosenthal, [47]). Let 1 < p < ∞, p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure such that L^p(μ) is not separable. Can L^p(μ) be a subspace of a Banach space having unconditional basis?

accepted.question_text: Let 2 < p < ∞, and let X be a subspace of an L^p space that does not contain a copy of ℓ^p(ω_1). Must there exist a finite measure μ such that X embeds into L^p(μ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2 (Johnson-Schechtman, [73]). Let 2 < p < ∞ and let X be a subspace of an L^p space such that X does not contain ℓ^p(ω_1). Does X embed into L^p(μ) for some finite measure μ?

accepted.question_text: Let 2 < p < ∞ and let μ be a finite measure. Is the Banach space L^p(μ) Hilbert generated, meaning that some Hilbert space H admits a bounded linear operator T: H → L^p(μ) with dense range?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.3. Let 2 < p < ∞ and let μ be a finite measure. Is L^p(μ) Hilbert generated?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach lattice for which there exists a weakly compact set L ⊆ X whose generated sublattice is dense in X. Must X be weakly compactly generated, that is, must there exist a weakly compact set K ⊆ X with X = span(K)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.4 (Diestel, [36]). Let X be a Banach lattice for which there is a weakly compact set L ⊆ X such that the sublattice generated by L is dense in X. Is X WCG?

accepted.question_text: If K is an infinite weakly Radon-Nikodym compact space, meaning that K is homeomorphic to a weak*-compact subset of the dual of a Banach space not containing ℓ^1, must K contain a non-stationary convergent sequence?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.5 (Haydon, [70]). Does every WRN (infinite) compact admit a convergent (non-stationary) sequence?

accepted.question_text: Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that there exists a separable Banach space X for which the partially ordered set K(B_X) of weakly compact subsets of the closed unit ball B_X, ordered by inclusion, is not Tukey equivalent to any of the four standard types {0}, N^N, K(Q), or the family of finite subsets of the continuum?
accepted.context_brief: Tukey types of weakly compact sets

evidence.quote: Problem 1.6. Is it relatively consistent that there is a separable Banach space X such that K(B_X) is not Tukey equivalent to {0}, N^N, K(Q) or [𝔠]^{<N}?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. Must X have the Gelfand-Phillips property, meaning that every limited subset of X is relatively norm compact?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.7. Let X be a Banach space not containing c_0. Does X have the Gelfand-Phillips property?

accepted.question_text: What is the smallest cardinal κ for which there exists a family of κ Banach spaces, each having property (K), such that their ℓ^1-direct sum fails property (K), where property (K) means that every weak*-null sequence in the dual admits a convex block subsequence converging to 0 in the Mackey topology?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.8. What is the least cardinality of a family of Banach spaces with property (K) whose ℓ^1-sum fails such property?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete. Must X have property (K), meaning that every weak*-null sequence in X* has a convex block subsequence converging to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.9. Let X be a separable Banach space which is weakly sequentially complete. Does X have property (K)?

accepted.question_text: For a Banach space X, is property D′ equivalent to property D? Here property D means that Ba(X, σ(X, Γ)) = Ba(X, w) for every total set Γ ⊆ X*, and property D′ means that every weak*-sequentially closed linear subspace of X* is weak*-closed.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 (Plichko, [103]). Is property D′ equivalent to property D?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a compact space such that the Baire sigma-algebras Ba(C(K), T_p) and Ba(C(K), w) coincide, where T_p is the topology of pointwise convergence on K. Must every probability measure in P(K) belong to the weak*-sequential closure Seq(co(Δ_K)) of the convex hull of the point-evaluation measures Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K}?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Let K be compact such that Ba(C(K), T_p) = Ba(C(K), w). Does the equality Seq(co(Δ_K)) = P(K) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let K be compact. Is the weak Baire measurability of the supremum norm on C(K), viewed as measurability with respect to Ba(C(K), w), equivalent to weak*-separability of the dual unit ball B_{C(K)^*} or of the whole dual space C(K)^*?
accepted.context_brief: Weak Baire measurability of the supremum norm

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Let K be compact. Is the measurability of ||·||_∞ with respect to Ba(C(K), w) equivalent to the weak*-separability of B_{C(K)^*} or C(K)^*?

accepted.question_text: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) differ, so Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Must there exist a norm-discrete subset of C(K) that is not weak-Borel, that is, does not belong to Bo(C(K), w)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4 (Burke-Pol, [17]). Let K be compact such that Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Is there a norm discrete subset of C(K) which does not belong to Bo(C(K), w)?

accepted.question_text: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) coincide, so Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)). Does it follow that the pointwise and norm Borel sigma-algebras also coincide, meaning Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K))?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5 (Marciszewski-Pol, [87]). Let K be compact such that Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)). Does the equality Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K)) hold?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a probability measure defined on the weak Borel sigma-algebra Bo(ℓ_∞, w) that does not admit any extension to a probability measure on the norm Borel sigma-algebra Bo(ℓ_∞)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6 (Fremlin, [57]). Is there a probability on Bo(ℓ_∞, w) which cannot be extended to a probability on Bo(ℓ_∞)?

accepted.question_text: Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a multifunction from a complete probability space into the nonempty subsets of a Banach space X. If F has convex closed values and is scalarly measurable, meaning F^{-}(H) is measurable for every open half-space H ⊆ X, must F admit a selector f: Ω → X that is itself scalarly measurable?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7. Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a scalarly measurable multi-function with convex closed values. Does F admit scalarly measurable selectors?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a Banach space X has density ω_1. Does the family wk(X) of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X have property (SC), meaning that there exists a set selector ψ on wk(X) such that ψ ∘ F is scalarly measurable for every scalarly measurable multifunction F with values in wk(X)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8 (Fremlin, [59]). Suppose dens(X) = ω_1. Does wk(X) have property (SC)?

accepted.question_text: Does the family cwk(X) of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of a Banach space X have property (SC), meaning that one can choose a selector on cwk(X) whose composition with every scalarly measurable multifunction into cwk(X) is scalarly measurable?
accepted.context_brief: Property (SC) for convex weakly compact sets

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9 (Fremlin, [59]). Does the family cwk(X) of all convex weakly compact non-empty subsets of X have property (SC)?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the Banach spaces with the Lebesgue property, meaning those spaces X for which every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is continuous almost everywhere.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. Characterize Banach spaces having the LP.

accepted.question_text: For which cardinals κ does the Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property, meaning that every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → ℓ_2(κ) is weakly continuous almost everywhere?
accepted.context_brief: Weak Lebesgue property for Hilbert spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. For which cardinals κ does the space ℓ_2(κ) have the WLP?

accepted.question_text: Let f: [0, 1] → c_0 be bounded, and let I(f) denote the set of all limits of sequences of Riemann sums of f taken over partitions whose diameters tend to 0. Must I(f) always be convex?
accepted.context_brief: Convexity of limit sets of Riemann sums

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 (Kadets-Kadets, [74]). Is the set I(f) convex for any bounded function f: [0, 1] → c_0?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a Banach space X has the Pettis integrability property, meaning that every scalarly bounded and scalarly measurable X-valued function is Pettis integrable. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure ν_f be separable?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4 (Plebanek, [102]). Suppose X has the PIP. Is R(ν_f) separable for every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X?

accepted.question_text: Suppose μ is a quasi-Radon probability measure. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure be relatively norm compact in X?
accepted.context_brief: Norm compactness for quasi-Radon Pettis ranges

evidence.quote: Problem 3.5 (Fremlin, [56]). Suppose μ is quasi-Radon. Is R(ν_f) relatively norm compact for every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a Banach space X does not contain a copy of c_0. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure be relatively norm compact?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6 (Talagrand, [121]). Suppose X does not contain c_0. Is R(ν_f) relatively norm compact for every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-uniform Eberlein compact space K such that C(K) belongs to the class U of Banach spaces for which every Pettis integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is McShane integrable? Equivalently, are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K = {K : C(K) ∈ U}?
accepted.context_brief: Non-uniform Eberlein compacta in class K

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K?

accepted.question_text: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?
accepted.context_brief: Topology dependence of the McShane integral

evidence.quote: Problem 3.8 (Fremlin, [56]). Let f: Ω → X be a function defined in a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) and taking values in a Banach space X. Let T_1 and T_2 be two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon. Suppose f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1. Is f McShane integrable with respect to T_2?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the closed unit ball B_X is contained in the range of some X-valued countably additive vector measure.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Characterize the Banach spaces X for which B_X is contained in the range of an X-valued vector measure.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a weakly compact subset of c_0. Must there exist a c_0-valued countably additive vector measure whose range contains K?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly compact subsets of c_0 as vector-measure ranges

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 (Anantharaman-Diestel, [4]). Let K be a weakly compact subset of c_0. Is K contained in the range of a c_0-valued vector measure?

accepted.question_text: Let ν_1 and ν_2 be vector measures of finite variation with the same range R(ν_1) = R(ν_2), and assume that both variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect. Must ν_1 and ν_2 have the same Pettis differentiability behavior with respect to their own variations?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3 (Rodríguez-Piazza - Romero-Moreno, [111]). Let ν_1 and ν_2 be vector measures of finite variation such that R(ν_1) = R(ν_2). Suppose further that |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect measures. Do ν_1 and ν_2 have the same Pettis differentiability character with respect to their variations?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space that does not contain a copy of ℓ_1, and let ν be an X-valued vector measure whose integration operator I_ν: L^1(ν) → X is completely continuous. Must ν have finite variation?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4 (Okada - Ricker - Rodríguez-Piazza, [99]). Let X be a Banach space not containing ℓ_1 and let ν be an X-valued vector measure such that I_ν is completely continuous. Does ν have finite variation?

accepted.question_text: Suppose ν is a non-atomic vector measure. Do there exist a set Γ and a vector measure ν̃: Σ → c_0(Γ) such that the associated spaces of integrable functions coincide, namely L^1(ν) = L^1(ν̃)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5 (Lipecki, [84]). Suppose ν is non-atomic. Are there a set Γ and a vector measure ν̃: Σ → c_0(Γ) such that L^1(ν) = L^1(ν̃)?

accepted.question_text: Characterize when the norming set Γ = {γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*}} is a James boundary of L^1(ν), meaning that every f ∈ L^1(ν) attains its norm at some functional γ_{g,x*} in Γ.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.6. Characterize when Γ is a James boundary of L^1(ν).

accepted.question_text: If the dual unit ball B_{X^*} is weak*-sequentially compact, must the dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} of the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) also be weak*-sequentially compact?
accepted.context_brief: Weak-star sequential compactness in Lebesgue-Bochner duals

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1. Is B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} weak*-sequentially compact if B_{X^*} is?

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 (Schlüchtermann-Wheeler, [113]). Is the space L^1(μ, X) SWCG whenever X is?

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly K-analytic, or strongly weakly countably determined, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) inherit the same corresponding property?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.3. Is the space L^p(μ, X) strongly WKA (resp. strongly WCD) whenever X is?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.4. Characterize those Banach spaces X such that L^p([0, 1], X) has unconditional basis (1 < p < ∞).

accepted.question_text: For which separable Banach spaces X are the Hilbertian sum ℓ_2(X) and the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_2([0, 1], X) isomorphic as Banach spaces?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.5 (Diestel, [34]). For which separable Banach spaces X are the spaces ℓ_2(X) and L_2([0, 1], X) isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: For which separable Banach spaces X does the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_1([0, 1], X) contain a subspace isomorphic to ℓ_2(X)?
accepted.context_brief: Copies of ℓ_2(X) inside L_1([0,1], X)

evidence.quote: Problem 5.6 (Diestel, [34]). For which separable Banach spaces X does L_1([0, 1], X) contain a copy of ℓ_2(X)?

accepted.question_text: For which Banach spaces X are the spaces ℓ_∞(X) and L_∞([0, 1], X) isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.7 (Cembranos-Mendoza, [26]). When are ℓ_∞(X) and L_∞([0, 1], X) isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: Does L^1[0, 1] have property (D_∞), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → L^1[0, 1] which is bounded in L^∞([0, 1], L^1[0, 1]) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 admits a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.8 (Dilworth-Girardi, [40]). Does L^1[0, 1] have property (D_∞)?

accepted.question_text: Are there infinite-dimensional reflexive Banach spaces with property (D_1), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → X which is bounded in L^1([0, 1], X) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 has a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.9 (Dilworth-Girardi, [40]). Are there reflexive (infinite-dimensional) Banach spaces with property (D_1)?
